Turn on light source to start exploring.

The Play Area contains a light source aimed at a sample of hydrogen atoms. The observation window displays a zoomed-in view of a single atom, which varies with the mode of exploration. In Model mode, there are various quantum models of the hydrogen atom to explore. In Experiment mode, the atom’s structure is a mystery and is obscured. Determine the structure of the hydrogen atom by shining white or monochromatic light on the sample. Observe changes in the electron’s state in the Electron Energy Level diagram.

controls.MODELS_OF_THE_HYDROGEN_ATOM/lInfo: {{l}}, the Angular Quantum Number, describes the shape of the orbital. Orbital shapes are spherical ({{l}} = 0 or {{s}}), peanut-shaped ({{l}} = 1 or {{p}}), and become more complex as {{l}} increases.
controls.MODELS_OF_THE_HYDROGEN_ATOM/mInfo: {{m}}, the Magnetic Quantum Number, describes the orientation of the orbital in space.
controls.MODELS_OF_THE_HYDROGEN_ATOM/nInfo: {{n}}, the Principal Quantum Number, describes the electron's energy and its probable distance from the nucleus.
controls.MODELS_OF_THE_HYDROGEN_ATOM/nlmInfo: The Schrödinger model uses 3 quantum numbers ({{n}},{{l}},{{m}}) to describe the most probable location of an electron, also known as an orbital.
